tasks.prompt: Order the handover of a new subdivision sewer system into the asset register.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: a developer built 6 km of sewers and a small lift station, and the city assumes ownership after the maintenance period if the assets meet standard.

cards.label: Confirm corrections are complete by reinspection of the listed defects, not by the developer statement alone
Start the new assets on the standard cleaning, inspection, and station maintenance cycles from the assumption date
Field verify a sample of manholes, station equipment, and easement access against the drawings
Review the CCTV and test records and list every defect the developer must correct before assumption, with locations and standards cited
Confirm the required submissions, including as built drawings, CCTV of every reach, station manuals, and test records, against the assumption checklist
Load the accepted assets into the register and maps with age starting at assumption, warranty dates, and the station spares and keys received

tasks.explanation: Assumption is the one moment the city can require proof, so defects are listed from records and corrected before ownership transfers. Loading warranty dates and starting maintenance cycles at handover prevents new assets becoming orphans in the system.

tasks.prompt: Order a lift station reliability improvement program for the fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 22 stations produce very uneven alarm and failure records, and the program must raise the worst performers first.

cards.label: Diagnose the dominant failure causes at each selected station, separating pump, control, power, level sensing, and wet well causes
Extend the program to the next group only when the first group shows sustained improvement, and record what worked for reuse
Build the fleet failure picture from alarm logs, callouts, overflow records, and repair history for the last three years
Track the selected stations monthly on callouts and alarms and compare with their own baseline, not the fleet average
Rank stations by failure frequency and consequence, and select the worst group for the first program year
Fund the fixes by cause, such as control upgrades, float replacement, or ventilation, rather than a uniform spend per station

tasks.explanation: Reliability money follows diagnosed causes, not equal shares. Comparing each station with its own baseline prevents a chronically bad station looking acceptable beside a worse fleet average.

tasks.prompt: Order the standby power testing program for all lift stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: stations have fixed generators or portable generator connections, and testing must prove real load carrying, not just engine starting.

cards.label: Correct deficiencies by risk, with stations lacking any backup or with failed transfer at the top of the list
Inventory the power arrangement at each station, including generator size, transfer switch type, fuel type, and portable connection compatibility
File test records per station and set the fleet report that lists any station currently without proven backup power
Schedule load tests so each generator carries the station actual pumping load, with the test timed to avoid high inflow periods
Confirm fuel storage, cold weather starting aids, and exercise timers at each site during the same visit cycle
During each test, record transfer time, voltage and frequency stability, fuel use, alarms, and any pump that fails to restart

tasks.explanation: A generator that starts but cannot carry both pumps is decoration. The fleet report naming stations without proven backup converts test paperwork into a risk the utility can act on.

tasks.prompt: Order a pump redundancy and firm capacity verification across duplex and triplex stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: growth and pump wear may have eroded firm capacity, the capacity with the largest pump out of service, at several stations.

cards.label: Run timed drawdown tests with each pump alone and with combinations, at stations where records suggest capacity has fallen
Program the corrections, from pump renewal to I/I work in the catchment, with the station risk stated for each
Compare measured firm capacity with peak inflow and flag stations where the margin is below the utility standard
Record verified firm capacity in the station file and set the retest interval based on growth rate in each catchment
List each station design firm capacity and the current peak inflow estimate from monitoring and run hour records
Investigate flagged stations for pump wear, force main restriction, or inflow growth as the cause of the shortfall

tasks.explanation: Firm capacity is the only honest capacity number for a station that must survive a pump failure. Attributing a shortfall to wear, restriction, or growth matters because each cause has a different fix and budget.

tasks.prompt: Order a level sensing upgrade program for stations with repeat float failures.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: eight stations generate most float related alarms, causing both missed starts and dry running risk.

cards.label: Monitor alarm counts at upgraded stations for three months against their prior record and report the change to the program file
Select the sensing arrangement per station, keeping independent high level float protection in every design
Confirm from alarm and work records that level sensing, not pumps or power, is the dominant failure cause at each candidate station
Install and commission station by station, proving start, stop, lag, and alarm levels over real pump cycles before handover
Standardize the successful arrangement as the fleet specification for future station renewals
Survey each wet well for grease loading, turbulence at the inflow, and mounting options for a continuous level device with float backup

tasks.explanation: Upgrading the wrong component is the common failure of reliability programs, so the cause is proven from records first. Keeping independent float backup means the new device can fail without removing the last protection.

tasks.prompt: Order the force main condition and reliability program startup.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the fleet has 31 force mains, the oldest are ductile iron and cast iron from the 1970s, and two have failed in five years.

cards.label: Set the reassessment cycle and record each main risk rating in the asset register so capital planning sees force mains beside gravity sewers
Rank mains by failure consequence, including discharge volume before isolation, watercourse proximity, and whether the station has any alternate path
Select the highest risk mains for detailed assessment, which may include pressure transient review and targeted excavation at fittings
Build the force main inventory with material, age, diameter, length, pressure class, and failure and repair history for each main
Gather the operating evidence available without excavation, such as pump pressure trends, air release valve condition, and surge history
Add protective measures where assessment supports them, such as surge control, air valve renewal, or cathodic protection checks

tasks.explanation: Force mains fail suddenly and discharge under pressure, so consequence dominates the ranking. Pressure trends and air valve condition are cheap evidence that is usually already available before any digging is justified.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet well and station cleaning frequency optimization study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: stations are cleaned on a fixed quarterly cycle, yet some wells foul in weeks and others are clean at every visit.

cards.label: Set trial intervals per group, shorter for fast fouling stations and longer where wells stay clean, with float checks kept frequent regardless
Extract cleaning records and fouling findings per station for two years, including grease depth, grit volume, and float fouling found
Review alarm and ragging events during the trial to confirm longer intervals did not trade cleaning savings for failures
Adopt the final intervals per station group and load them into the maintenance system with the evidence attached
Brief cleaning crews to record findings in the same format during the trial so intervals can be compared fairly
Group stations by fouling rate and identify the catchment features that predict fast fouling, such as food service density and flat upstream sewers

tasks.explanation: Fixed intervals overclean clean wells and underclean dirty ones. The trial guards the obvious trap, that saving cleaning visits must not be repaid as float failures and callouts.

tasks.prompt: Order the alarm rationalization review for the station monitoring system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operators receive hundreds of alarms a month, many are repeats or nuisance alarms, and real events risk being lost in the noise.

cards.label: Extract the alarm history and rank alarms by frequency, station, and type, and identify alarms that never lead to any action
Adjust setpoints, delays, and alarm routing with the control staff so critical alarms, such as high level and power fail, stand out by priority
Record the alarm philosophy adopted, including which alarms call out after hours, in the station operations manual
Fix the real faults found, since a repeated alarm is often an unrepaired defect announcing itself
Classify each frequent alarm as a real recurring fault, a setpoint or delay problem, a faulty device, or information that belongs in a daily report, not an alarm
Monitor alarm counts and operator response times for two months after the changes and compare with the baseline

tasks.explanation: Deleting nuisance alarms without fixing the faults behind the frequent ones hides real defects. Priority separation is the goal, so the alarms that protect against overflows are impossible to confuse with information.

tasks.prompt: Order a station obsolescence and renewal plan for controls and electrical gear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: several stations run control panels and starters the manufacturers no longer support, and failures are repaired with salvaged parts.

cards.label: Commission each renewed station with full functional testing of alternation, alarms, and backup power transfer before acceptance
Update the fleet standard and the spares list from the renewed design and retire the salvaged parts practice for renewed stations
Rank stations by the risk of an unrepairable control failure, weighted by station criticality and whether manual operation is possible
Inventory control and electrical equipment by station with age, manufacturer support status, and spare parts availability
Sequence the packages so the highest risk stations are renewed first, with temporary control provisions planned for each changeover
Group renewals into packages that share a standard panel design so spares, training, and documentation stay common across the fleet

tasks.explanation: Unsupported controls are a reliability debt that fails without warning. A standard panel design across packages compounds the benefit, because every renewal then reduces the spares and training burden for the whole fleet.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a station that repeatedly overflows in extreme storms despite sound pumps.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the station equipment tests well, yet the wet well surcharges in the largest storms and has overflowed twice in three years.

cards.label: Compare the event inflow with the station firm capacity and the catchment design flow to confirm the shortfall is hydraulic, not mechanical
Evaluate options on the same event basis, including catchment I/I removal, added storage, pump or force main capacity, and controlled development limits
Reconstruct the two overflow events from level records, rain data, pump run logs, and the timeline of operator actions
Record the analysis in the capacity assurance file so the next event is judged against a plan, not improvised
Quantify the excess volume that arrived above firm capacity and how long storage in the wet well and upstream sewers delayed the overflow
Recommend the staged plan with the trigger for capital work, and interim measures such as pre storm drawdown and portable pump deployment points

tasks.explanation: Sound pumps overflowing means the problem is inflow against capacity, and the event reconstruction proves it with numbers. Interim measures matter because capital work takes years while the next extreme storm does not wait.

tasks.prompt: Order a contractor preventive maintenance quality audit for lift stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a contractor performs quarterly station preventive maintenance under contract, and the utility wants evidence the visits deliver the specified work.

cards.label: Raise the discrepancies with the contractor in writing, tied to the specification clauses, and require a correction plan
Report the audit outcome to management and adjust the specification or inspection frequency for the next contract term
Compare run hours, alarm history, and deficiency reports with the checklist claims to find work reported but not evident
Visit a sample of stations shortly after a completed visit and check the items the checklist claims, such as valve exercise, float cleaning, and generator exercise records
Define the audit sample across stations and quarters and pull the contractor completed checklists for those visits
Reinspect the corrected items and apply the contract remedies for any work still not delivered

tasks.explanation: Checklists prove attendance, not work, so the audit verifies physical evidence at the station. Tying discrepancies to specification clauses keeps the correction contractual rather than personal.

tasks.prompt: Order the design of a risk based CCTV inspection cycle for the whole network.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the network is 820 km, the camera fleet can inspect about 90 km a year, and inspection must follow risk rather than a fixed rotation alone.

cards.label: Check the class lengths against the annual camera capacity and adjust cycles or capacity until the program is actually deliverable
Refresh the classes annually from new grades and failures so a deteriorating district moves itself into a shorter cycle
Divide the network into inspection classes by criticality, age and material, known defect history, and consequence of failure
Track completion and findings by class each quarter and report any class falling behind its cycle to management
Set a target cycle for each class, with the highest risk class inspected most often and low risk modern pipe on the longest cycle
Build the first three years of routes by area so cleaning, traffic control, and camera work are coordinated street by street

tasks.explanation: A cycle the fleet cannot deliver is a fiction, so capacity is checked against class lengths before routes are promised. Annual refresh from findings lets deterioration, not habit, set the next cycle.

tasks.prompt: Order a manhole condition assessment program for trunk sewer structures.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: 3400 manholes exist, trunk structures are assessed first, and assessments use a standard form covering cover, frame, chimney, wall, benching, and invert.

cards.label: Record each assessment with photos of defects and a safety note for structures needing confined space precautions at the next visit
Define the assessment form and defect terms with photo examples so different crews grade the same defect the same way
Audit a sample of assessments each season by reinspection and correct any systematic grading drift between crews
Train and calibrate assessors on a set of structures assessed in common, and compare their grades before field work starts
Convert the grades into work, separating immediate safety repairs, infiltration sealing, and structures for renewal planning
Sequence the field work by basin with the cleaning and CCTV program so structure and pipe condition for an area arrive together

tasks.explanation: Calibration on common structures is what makes grades from different crews comparable. The sample reaudit catches drift early, before a season of soft or harsh grading distorts the renewal program.

tasks.prompt: Order the condition assessment of a siphon crossing under a river.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a twin barrel siphon built in the 1960s carries a trunk sewer under a river, it cannot be taken out of service completely, and its condition is unknown.

cards.label: Plan the inspection around flow, isolating one barrel at a time if the design allows, with bypass or storage arrangements for the barrel under inspection
Assess the findings for remaining life and failure risk and compare the barrels, since twin barrels often deteriorate unevenly
Arrange the safety and environmental controls for work at the riverbanks and in the chambers, including atmosphere testing and spill containment
Set the cleaning and reinspection interval and any renewal project from the findings, and record the access lessons for the next crew
Gather the design drawings, past cleaning records, and any dive or inspection reports to establish what is known before mobilizing
Inspect the isolated barrel by the method its size and condition allow, recording sediment depth, joint condition, and structural defects

tasks.explanation: One barrel at a time keeps the trunk in service while producing real condition evidence. Comparing barrels matters because assuming the second matches the first is how siphon failures surprise utilities.

tasks.prompt: Order a smoke and dye testing assessment program for a cross connection district.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a mixed industrial and residential district shows storm flow in the sanitary sewer and sanitary traces in the storm system after rain.

cards.label: Classify each confirmed connection by the flow it admits and by whether it sits on private or public property under the local rule
Run smoke testing street by street and record every emergence, photographing and locating each suspected connection
Define the district boundaries from the flow evidence and list the properties and drainage features inside them
Confirm suspected connections with dye testing, introducing dye at the specific fixture or drain and watching the correct and incorrect systems
Issue the correction requirements for confirmed connections and schedule the flow remeasurement that will prove the district improvement
Notify property owners and occupants of the testing program, the dates, and how access to yards and cleanouts will be arranged

tasks.explanation: Smoke finds suspects and dye proves connections, and only proven connections justify a correction order. Classifying by flow admitted lets the biggest inflow sources be corrected first.

tasks.prompt: Order the acoustic and flow based screening program for blockage prone sewers.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility wants a fast screening method to direct CCTV and cleaning toward reaches with developing restrictions before they block.

cards.label: Report the program yield, including blockages found before failure and the inspection metres avoided on reaches that screened clear
Run the screening during comparable flow conditions and record the restriction score or flow anomaly for every reach in the same format
Clean reaches where the restriction is deposits rather than structure, and confirm the improvement by rescreening after cleaning
Select the screening reaches from blockage history, flat grades, and grease and root evidence, and record the baseline flow condition for each
Rank the reaches by screening result and send the worst group to CCTV for a graded condition record
Compare screening predictions with the CCTV findings and blockage calls over the season and adjust the screening threshold that triggers inspection

tasks.explanation: Screening earns its place by prediction accuracy, so its calls are checked against CCTV and real blockages. Rescreening after cleaning proves the restriction was deposits and closes that reach honestly.

tasks.prompt: Order a corrosion assessment program for sewers downstream of force main discharges.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: several concrete trunk reaches below force main discharge manholes show crown corrosion, and the program must size the problem before renewal money is committed.

cards.label: Inspect the ranked reaches by CCTV suited to crown assessment and record corrosion depth and extent in standard terms
Map the reaches downstream of each force main discharge and rank them by detention time in the force main, which drives sulfide generation
Cost the response options per reach, including chemical dosing at the station, ventilation, lining, and monitoring, using given rates
Set the monitoring points and reinspection dates for the monitored reaches and file the corrosion map with the asset register
Separate reaches needing protective action now from reaches that can be monitored, using remaining wall and structural evidence
Measure or review sulfide and pH evidence at the discharge points and at intervals downstream to find where attack is most aggressive

tasks.explanation: Sulfide generation follows force main detention, so the map starts there rather than with random inspection. Separating act now from monitor reaches prevents both premature lining and neglected advanced corrosion.

tasks.prompt: Order the condition data quality improvement project for legacy CCTV records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: fifteen years of surveys exist in mixed formats, some grades cannot be trusted, and rehabilitation planning depends on this data.

cards.label: Inventory the survey archive by year, format, contractor, and grading standard used, and list what cannot be opened or located at all
Prioritize resurvey of reaches whose legacy grades drive near term capital decisions or whose condition is effectively unknown
Publish the data confidence summary beside the condition summary so planners see both in every report
Set conversion or caution rules per era, such as treating one era grades as indicative only until resurveyed
Sample surveys from each era and regrade them against the current standard to measure how far legacy grades drift
Load the cleaned records into the asset system with the era and confidence attached to each grade

tasks.explanation: Legacy grades are not worthless, but they are not equal either, and the regrading sample measures the difference. Attaching confidence to each grade lets planning use old data with its eyes open.

tasks.prompt: Order a building service lateral condition program for older neighbourhoods.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: backup records suggest laterals in pre 1960 neighbourhoods are a growing failure source, but the city has almost no lateral condition data.

cards.label: Design the response options, from owner information to a cost shared renewal program, based on the condition picture found
Report the findings with the sample limits stated, so a small survey is not presented as a census of every lateral
Offer launch camera inspections from the mainline during the area CCTV program, with owner notification and consent handled in advance
Define the lateral study areas from backup history, home age, and mainline condition so the sample represents the wider housing stock
Analyse the sample to estimate the share of laterals in each condition band for the wider neighbourhoods
Record lateral condition in standard terms, noting material, joints, roots, and where responsibility changes at the property line

tasks.explanation: Sampling from the mainline program is the cheapest way to learn about laterals at scale. Stating the sample limits protects the program, because lateral policy built on overstated data will not survive contact with owners.

tasks.prompt: Order the rapid assessment after a sewer collapse is repaired on a collector street.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a 375 mm collector collapsed under a bus route, the repair is complete, and the utility must learn whether the collapse is isolated or a district warning.

cards.label: CCTV the reaches upstream and downstream of the repair and any parallel streets of the same age and material
Review other reaches of the same material, era, and soil conditions and rank them for early inspection
Secure the repair records, the failed pipe samples or photos, and the crew account of soil and groundwater conditions found in the excavation
Record the lessons in the assessment program file, including any change to grading guidance or inspection cycles for that pipe material
Compare the failure mode with the condition grades on file and check whether the failed reach had been graded better than it deserved
Complete the priority inspections and feed any severe findings directly into the rehabilitation ranking with the collapse noted as evidence

tasks.explanation: A collapse is free, unwelcome condition data about a whole pipe cohort, not just one reach. Checking whether the file grade overstated the failed pipe tests the grading system itself.

tasks.prompt: Order the integration of flow, condition, and failure data into one network health report.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: three data sets live in separate systems and management wants one annual network health picture for council.

cards.label: Present the measures by district so areas with converging bad signals, poor condition, high blockages, and high peaking, stand out together
Publish the report with the data confidence notes and archive the extracts so next year report is built the same way
Investigate the disagreements rather than averaging them, since a mismatch usually reveals a recording gap in one system
Extract each measure from its source system for the same reporting period and reconcile totals that disagree between systems
Define the health measures in advance, such as condition band shares, blockage rate per 100 km, overflow causes, and wet weather peaking trend
Link each adverse measure to the program responding to it, cleaning, rehabilitation, I/I, or capacity, with its current status

tasks.explanation: Converging signals are the report value, because one bad measure can mislead but three together rarely do. Reconciling disagreeing totals first keeps the council picture built on records that match.

tasks.prompt: Order a trunk sewer capacity study for a growing sewershed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: approved development will add 9000 people to the shed over 15 years, and two trunk reaches already run deep in large storms.

cards.label: Add the wet weather allowance from the measured rainfall response, including the I/I reduction the current program is expected to deliver
Recommend the staged capacity plan with construction triggers tied to development milestones rather than fixed dates alone
Establish the current flows from monitoring at the shed outlet and key branches, separating dry weather flow from wet weather response
Size the response options for the short reaches, including upsizing, parallel relief, storage, and further I/I removal, on given rates
Build the future dry weather flow from the approved development using given per capita flows and the phasing of the developments
Test each trunk reach against the future peak flow and list the reaches that surcharge, with the year the shortfall begins

tasks.explanation: Future flow is built from measured response, not textbook peaking alone, because this shed real behaviour is known. Triggers tied to development milestones keep capital from arriving years early or one storm late.

tasks.prompt: Order the design flow update for the whole collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the system design flows date from a study 12 years old, growth patterns have shifted, and several projects are being designed from stale numbers.

cards.label: Set the wet weather design allowances from the I/I studies, with higher allowances where removal programs are incomplete
Collect the current population, water use, and flow monitoring summaries for every shed, noting which sheds have real data and which rely on estimates
Brief the design teams on the changes and withdraw the old table from the design manual so stale numbers stop circulating
Recalculate dry weather design flows using given per capita and non residential allowances directed for the study
Issue the updated design flow table with the data basis stated for each shed and the date after which the table must be refreshed
Derive peaking factors from the monitoring record by shed size rather than applying one factor to the whole city

tasks.explanation: One peaking factor for every shed size misstates both small and large sheds, so factors come from the monitoring record. Withdrawing the old table is essential, because superseded numbers in circulation keep designing projects.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet weather storage feasibility study for a surcharging district.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a low lying district surcharges in large storms, upsizing the outfall crosses a river, and storage in a park site is the alternative to test.

cards.label: Confirm the usable storage volume at the park site from its area, depth limits, and the levels needed to fill and drain by gravity where possible
Compare storage with the outfall upsizing on given rates over the same service life and the same level of protection
Model the storage operation through the design storm, including fill rate, the peak shaved, and the drain down time before the next storm
Recommend the option with its residual risk stated, including what happens in a storm larger than the design event
Quantify the surcharge problem from level records and storm data, including the excess volume above the outfall capacity in the design storm
Check the operational needs, including odour control, cleaning access, screening of incoming flow, and safe overflow routing if the design storm is exceeded

tasks.explanation: Storage is sized from the measured excess volume, not from the site that happens to be available. Drain down time is checked because storage still full from the last storm protects against nothing.

tasks.prompt: Order the capacity review triggered by a major development application.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a developer proposes 2400 homes plus a school and commercial block at the edge of the city, draining to one lift station and trunk.

cards.label: Set the approval conditions, which may include phased occupancy tied to upgrade completion, in writing for the development file
Compare the added flow with the spare capacity of each element at the development build out year, including other approved developments on the same path
Calculate the development design flows using given allowances and peaking factors for its size and mix of uses
Identify the elements that fall short and the share of the upgrade cost attributable to this development under the city cost sharing rules
Record the committed flows in the capacity ledger so the next application on the same path starts from the true remaining capacity
Trace the flow path from the development through every reach, the lift station, and the force main to the treatment plant connection

tasks.explanation: Spare capacity must include every other approved development, not just the applicant in the room. The capacity ledger is the memory that prevents the same spare capacity being promised twice.

tasks.prompt: Order a sewer capacity ledger and allocation routine for development services.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planners, engineers, and developers currently quote different remaining capacities for the same trunks and stations.

cards.label: Audit the ledger annually against connections actually built, releasing allocations for developments that did not proceed
Load the current position from the latest studies and reconcile it with the development approvals issued in the last three years
Route every new application through the ledger so approvals add their flows at the moment they are granted
Define the ledger structure by element, with design capacity, current committed flow, and the flow reserved for infill and errors
Set the allocation rule, including how long an allocation is held for an approved development and when it returns to the pool
Publish a quarterly capacity statement for the constrained elements so applicants can see the position before they design

tasks.explanation: One ledger ends the three versions of the truth problem. The annual audit releasing dead allocations matters because reserved but unbuilt flow quietly sterilizes capacity the city actually has.

tasks.prompt: Order the climate allowance review for wet weather design standards.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: rainfall records show more intense short storms than the design standard assumes, and several recent surcharges occurred in storms below the old design size.

cards.label: Test the sensitive sheds with the revised events and list where the current system falls short of the intended protection level
Assemble the recent storm and surcharge record and compare the storms that caused problems with the current design storm definition
Recommend the standard the city should adopt, phased so the worst sheds are addressed first, with the residual risk of phasing stated
Record the adopted standard in the design manual with its review date, since rainfall data will keep moving
Estimate the program cost of restoring protection in the shortfall sheds using given rates for storage, upsizing, and I/I removal
Review the updated rainfall intensity data provided for the study and identify how the design events change for the durations that matter to sewers

tasks.explanation: The review starts from storms that actually caused surcharging, which grounds the statistics in service failures. A review date on the standard accepts that the climate input is a moving target, not a settled constant.

tasks.prompt: Order a lift station and force main capacity study for a regional trunk system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: three communities drain through one regional station and a 6 km force main, and growth in all three is testing the shared capacity.

cards.label: Meter or assemble flow records for each community contribution so the shared peak is understood by source, not just in total
Identify which element limits the system first and how much growth that limit accommodates under the agreed allocation between communities
Recommend the upgrade staging and the flow triggers that start design, and record the agreement in the regional capacity file
Check the wet well and any upstream storage for the balancing effect they provide during the combined peak
Test the station firm capacity and the force main velocity and pressure at the current and projected combined peaks
Cost the upgrade options for the limiting element using given rates and set out the cost sharing implied by each community share of the peak

tasks.explanation: Shared systems fail politically when contributions are argued from estimates, so each community flow is established first. Cost sharing follows measured peak share, which is the only basis all three can accept.

tasks.prompt: Order the infiltration allowance audit for new sewer construction standards.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: capacity studies assume new sewers add little infiltration, but flow records in two recent subdivisions suggest the allowance is optimistic.

cards.label: Recommend the revised design allowance and any tightened construction testing the evidence supports
Apply the revised allowance to the live capacity studies and note which project designs change as a result
Compare the measured infiltration per kilometre with the allowance used in design and with the construction test results recorded at acceptance
Select the newest subdivisions with reliable flow records and separate their dry weather flow into sanitary flow and base infiltration by night flow analysis
Relate the findings to construction and inspection practice, including testing methods and the timing of acceptance testing
Inspect a sample of the higher infiltration subdivisions for the likely entry points, such as manhole chimneys and lateral connections

tasks.explanation: Design allowances should be audited against built reality, because optimistic allowances compound across every new subdivision. Linking findings back to acceptance testing turns a capacity correction into a construction quality fix.

tasks.prompt: Order a surcharge risk mapping study for insurance and emergency planning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the city wants a map of where basements are at risk when sewers surcharge, to guide both capital priorities and resident advice.

cards.label: Add the physical risk factors, including low service elevations relative to the sewer, flat reaches, and known capacity shortfalls
Classify streets by risk band and check the classification against the insurance and complaint records for fairness
Combine the sewer level and surcharge records with the basement backup history to identify streets with proven surcharge exposure
Publish the internal map with its data limits stated and set the update cycle tied to new surcharge events and completed projects
Ground truth the draft map with the crews and long serving operators, who know streets that flood before any record shows it
Use the map to rank backwater valve advice, monitoring locations, and the capital projects that retire the most risk

tasks.explanation: Records alone miss streets that experienced crews know flood first, so ground truthing is a formal step. The map earns its keep by ranking the projects and advice that retire risk, not by sitting in a report.

tasks.prompt: Order the growth scenario planning session for the 25 year collection master plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the master plan must handle three growth scenarios, from slow infill to a major new suburb, without committing to one forecast.

cards.label: Cost each group using given rates and show the spending profile by scenario so finance sees the commitment shape
Schedule the plan refresh cycle and the indicators, such as connection rates by district, that the refresh will examine
Sort the responses into no regret work needed under every scenario, staged work with triggers, and work deferred unless the fast scenario arrives
Run the capacity tests for each scenario and identify the elements that fail in all three, in two, or only in the fastest growth case
Agree the three scenarios with planning staff, including population, location, and phasing for each, in writing before any modelling
Adopt the master plan with the trigger points and the monitoring that will reveal which scenario is unfolding

tasks.explanation: Scenarios prevent the master plan betting the utility on one forecast. No regret work proceeds at once, while scenario dependent work waits for triggers, which is how a 25 year plan stays both committed and flexible.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual confined space program review for collection operations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the program covers manholes, wet wells, siphons, and chambers, and the review must test the written program against field practice.

cards.label: Audit a sample of live entries against the procedure, covering atmosphere testing order, ventilation, attendant duties, and rescue readiness
Record the review, the corrections with owners and dates, and brief all crews on what changed and why
Inventory the confined spaces crews enter and confirm each is classified, signed, and covered by an entry procedure that matches its hazards
Correct the gaps found, from equipment and training to procedure steps that crews cannot perform as written
Review the year entry permits and incident and near miss reports for patterns, such as spaces where readings repeatedly change during entry
Check the rescue arrangements honestly, including whether the designated method and equipment can actually retrieve an entrant from the deepest spaces used

tasks.explanation: The rescue check is the review moment of truth, because a plan that cannot retrieve a worker from the deepest wet well is not a plan. Auditing live entries finds the gap between the written program and the real one.

tasks.prompt: Order the hydrogen sulfide control program for high risk collection locations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: force main discharge points, long flat trunks, and two stations have repeated sulfide readings, and worker exposure and corrosion share the same source.

cards.label: Set the work rules for the top locations, covering testing before and during work, ventilation setup, and when work stops and withdraws
List the high risk locations from gas monitoring records, odour complaints, and corrosion evidence, and rank them by readings and exposure frequency
Track readings and exposures quarterly and report whether controls are reducing the hazard or merely documenting it
Confirm the monitoring practice at each location, including fixed detectors where fitted, personal monitors, and the action levels crews use
Brief and drill the crews who work at these locations, using the actual readings history as the teaching material
Review the engineering controls in place, such as ventilation at stations and chemical dosing, and identify locations relying on procedures alone

tasks.explanation: Sulfide control is judged by falling readings, not by the number of procedures issued. Locations relying on procedures alone are named, because engineering controls protect workers who make a mistake, and procedures do not.

tasks.prompt: Order a traffic control program upgrade for work on arterial roads.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: cleaning and CCTV programs increasingly work on high speed arterials, and two recent near misses involved passing traffic.

cards.label: Compare the plans with the provincial traffic control requirements in general terms and with the actual road speeds and volumes where crews work
Audit live setups on arterials during the first season and correct deviations on the spot with the crew leader
Standardize the setups by work type, including lane closure, mobile work, and short duration stops, with equipment lists for each
Record the program changes and track traffic incidents and near misses as a standing dashboard measure
Review the near miss and incident records and the current traffic control plans used for each common work setup
Train and assess the crew members who set up and supervise traffic control, and restrict the role to those assessed as competent

tasks.explanation: Near misses are the data, and waiting for an injury to justify the upgrade is the failure this program avoids. Restricting setup supervision to assessed staff makes the standard real rather than advisory.

tasks.prompt: Order the contractor safety prequalification and monitoring routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: lining, CCTV, and construction contractors work in and around live sewers, and the utility is formalizing how their safety is managed.

cards.label: Review every contractor incident and near miss jointly and require the corrective actions to be shared across the contractor other crews
Brief awarded contractors on the site specific hazards, including gas risks, live flow, and the utility stop work authority, before mobilization
Define the prequalification evidence required for each work type, including confined space, traffic control, and bypass pumping competence
Inspect contractor work in progress against the agreed controls, with findings recorded and correction times set by risk
Score contractor safety performance into the record used at the next procurement so field performance affects future awards
Review submissions before award and reject or condition any contractor whose evidence does not match the hazards of the work bid

tasks.explanation: Prequalification that is never checked in the field is paperwork. Feeding field performance into the next procurement is what gives the whole routine its leverage.

tasks.prompt: Order the lockout and energy control program review for lift stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: stations contain electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and stored pressure energy, and several panels predate the current lockout standard.

cards.label: Update the program file with the audit results and the equipment changes still outstanding
Write or revise the station specific lockout steps where the generic procedure does not match the installed equipment
Train and observe each crew performing the lockout for their common tasks and correct technique during the observation
Walk each station type and list every energy source that must be controlled for the common tasks, including pump work, valve work, and panel work
Fit the lock points, valves, and blanks the steps require, since a procedure naming a lock point that does not exist will be bypassed
Audit lockout use on unannounced visits during the season and record compliance by station type, not by individual blame

tasks.explanation: Station specific steps matter because no two older stations isolate the same way. Fitting the physical lock points is part of the procedure, not an afterthought, or the written steps will quietly stop being followed.

tasks.prompt: Order the safety investigation follow up for a serious near miss during bypass pumping.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a bypass hose coupling failed under pressure during a night repair, no one was injured, and management requires the lessons to change practice.

cards.label: Identify the causes in layers, from the immediate equipment failure through the inspection practice to the specification that allowed the coupling type
Secure the failed equipment and the scene records, including photos, the setup diagram, and the crew statements taken while memory is fresh
Brief every crew that performs bypass work on the findings and the new checks, and update the bypass procedure the same week
Verify at the next two bypass setups that the new checks are performed, and close the investigation only after that field verification
Set corrective actions for each layer, including equipment standards, a pre pressurization check, and exclusion zones during testing
Reconstruct the event timeline, covering hose and coupling selection, pressure reached, inspection before pressurizing, and where each worker stood

tasks.explanation: Layered causes prevent the easy answer that a coupling simply failed. Closing the investigation only after field verification stops corrective actions existing solely in the report.

tasks.prompt: Order the winter work safety program for collection crews.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: prairie winter work combines extreme cold, ice at manholes, frozen equipment, and short daylight, and the program is set before the season.

cards.label: Review last winter incidents, injuries, and equipment damage and list the tasks and conditions that produced them
Brief all crews before the season and confirm supervisors hold the authority and the expectation to stop work that cannot be done safely
Record the season results and carry the lessons into the next year program rather than rediscovering them each November
Prepare the equipment program, covering manhole ice removal, ladder and platform gritting, hose and pump freeze protection, and vehicle winter kits
Set the cold exposure rules, including work and warming cycles, the buddy check routine, and the conditions that stop outdoor work
Monitor compliance and incidents through the season with a mid winter review that adjusts the rules while they still matter

tasks.explanation: A mid winter review is what separates a program from a poster, because the rules can still be fixed while the season runs. Supervisor stop work authority is stated out loud so it is used on the day it is needed.

tasks.prompt: Order a trenching and excavation safety review for sewer repair crews.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: repair crews open excavations weekly, often in wet soils near the river valley, and a recent inspection found inconsistent shoring practice.

cards.label: Arrange the additional equipment or method changes the audit shows are needed, such as different box sizes for deep wet work
Record the review findings and track excavation audit results as a standing safety measure
Compare the protective systems available, shoring, shielding, and sloping, with the depths and soils in the records and list any job type the equipment cannot cover
Review the excavation records and the soil and depth conditions the crews actually meet across the districts
Audit live excavations across districts and correct protective system and access deficiencies before work continues in them
Confirm the competent person designations and that inspections occur at the start of each shift and after rain or thaw changes conditions

tasks.explanation: Protective systems must match the soils and depths crews actually meet, not the catalogue case. Inspections after rain or thaw are singled out because changed conditions are when sound looking trench walls fail.

tasks.prompt: Order the new operator safety mentorship structure for collection crews.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: six new operators start this year across cleaning, CCTV, and station crews, and informal shadowing has produced uneven habits.

cards.label: Assign each new operator a named mentor and schedule the supervised repetitions each high risk task requires before sign off
Review progress monthly with the crew leaders and adjust assignments where a new operator is advancing faster or needs more support
Define the tasks a new operator may perform alone, under supervision, or not at all, by crew and by stage of their first year
Evaluate the structure at year end from incident, near miss, and supervisor feedback and revise the task lists for the next intake
Use a sign off record per task, signed by the mentor after observed performance, not by time served
Restrict high risk work, such as confined space entry and live electrical tasks, until the specific sign offs are complete, without exception

tasks.explanation: Sign off by observed performance, not time served, is the structure core. The no exception rule for high risk tasks protects new operators from the informal pressure to help beyond their training.

tasks.prompt: Order the emergency equipment readiness program for collection operations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: gas detectors, rescue gear, bypass pumps, and spill kits live across depots and trucks, and readiness has depended on individual habit.

cards.label: Set the storage standard so equipment is reachable and complete at the start of a shift, not distributed across vehicles
Report readiness monthly as the share of items in date and serviceable, with failed items named until they are corrected
Run the first full check cycle and repair or replace what fails, including detector calibration and rescue gear inspection
Assign a named owner for each equipment group at each depot, responsible for the checks and for removing failed items from service
Inventory the emergency equipment by location and set the inspection and calibration standard each item carries
Drill with the equipment quarterly, since readiness includes crews who can deploy it in the dark and in winter, not just equipment that works

tasks.explanation: Readiness is equipment plus crews who can use it under bad conditions, which is why drills are part of the program. Naming failed items in the monthly report until corrected prevents quiet expiry from becoming the norm.

tasks.prompt: Order the response leadership sequence for a major trunk sewer overflow at a watercourse.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk main has failed beside a creek in a storm, sewage is reaching the water, and the senior operator takes command of the response.

cards.label: Make the required notifications in general terms to the provincial regulator, public health contacts, and downstream users the procedure lists
Stand down in stages as flow is controlled, and open the event review file while records and memories are fresh
Confirm the overflow location, the estimated rate, and that the watercourse is affected, and take command with a named deputy and a log keeper
Organize the repair and the cleanup in parallel, including contaminated material handling and the sampling the procedure requires
Stop or reduce the discharge first, by bypass pumping, plugging, or diverting flow, using the preplanned access and equipment points
Protect the public with signage, trail and road closures at the affected area, and a single spokesperson for information

tasks.explanation: Flow control comes before everything except confirming the event, because every minute of delay is volume in the creek. A named log keeper from the start is what makes the later regulatory account and the review possible.

tasks.prompt: Order a bypass pumping plan for a planned trunk sewer repair.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a trunk reach must be isolated for two days, peak flow in the reach is known from monitoring, and a school and a clinic sit upstream.

cards.label: Staff the bypass continuously with operators who can refuel, respond to alarms, and restart pumps, with relief shifts planned for the full duration
Calculate the bypass duty from the peak flow expected during the repair window, including a wet weather allowance if rain is forecast
Remove the isolation only after the repair is accepted, then stand the bypass down in stages and record the flows and any incidents
Size the pumps with redundancy, so the duty is met with the largest pump out of service, and confirm suction and discharge routes and hose or pipe sizes
Isolate the reach and carry out the repair while the bypass performance and upstream levels are monitored and logged
Set up and test the full bypass under flow before the sewer is isolated, proving couplings, fuel, alarms, and the changeover to standby pumps

tasks.explanation: The bypass is proven under real flow before isolation, because discovering an undersized pump after the plugs are in is the classic disaster. Redundancy sized to the largest unit out is the same firm capacity logic as a lift station.

tasks.prompt: Order the overflow volume estimation and reporting routine for a completed event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. cards.label: Select the estimation method that fits the evidence, such as level and duration with a rated overflow path, pump records, or upstream flow data
Submit the report within the time the procedure requires in general terms, with the cause, volume, receiving environment, and actions taken
Calculate the volume with the assumptions written beside it, including the flow rate used for each period of the event
File the method and the working in the event record so the next event is estimated the same way and the figure can be defended later
Reconstruct the start and stop times from level records, alarm logs, crew reports, and resident calls, and resolve conflicts between sources
Have a second operator check the reconstruction and the arithmetic before the figure leaves the utility

tasks.explanation: A defensible volume states its method and assumptions, because no overflow is metered directly. The second check happens before submission, since correcting a regulator report afterwards damages credibility more than a careful first figure.

tasks.prompt: Order the after action review for a night of multiple storm overflows.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one storm produced overflows at five locations, two basement backup clusters, and a station high level event, all in nine hours.

cards.label: Assign corrective actions with owners and dates, separating quick procedure fixes from capital items for the capacity program
Identify the decisions that helped, such as pre storm drawdown or crew prepositioning, so they become standard practice rather than luck
Build the single event timeline from dispatch, alarm, level, and crew records across all locations before opinions are gathered
Identify the failures in layers, covering capacity, equipment, staffing, communications, and information available to dispatch
Brief all shifts on the findings and track the actions in the CMOM file until each is closed or formally accepted as a risk
Separate what the storm imposed from what the system and the response controlled, location by location

tasks.explanation: One timeline for the whole night reveals system behaviour that five separate reports would miss. Crediting the decisions that helped is deliberate, because reviews that only list failures teach crews to hide improvisation that actually works.

tasks.prompt: Order a flood season readiness program for the collection system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the spring freshet and storm season raises river levels, groundwater, and inflow together, and readiness work starts six weeks ahead.

cards.label: Review readiness weekly through the season and stand the program down only after river and groundwater levels return to normal
Inspect and prepare the listed assets, sealing covers in flood areas, testing station backup power, and clearing access routes
Confirm the staffing plan, including call out rosters, mutual aid contacts, and the thresholds that trigger prepositioning crews
List the assets and locations exposed to the season, including riverside manholes, low stations, siphon chambers, and known surcharge districts
Stage the response equipment, bypass pumps, hoses, plugs, generators, and spill material, at the depots nearest the exposed areas
Brief supervisors and dispatch on the season forecast, the trigger levels, and the notification steps in general terms

tasks.explanation: Readiness is sequenced to the season, not to the first flood call. Trigger levels agreed in advance turn a rising river into a planned mobilization instead of a debate.

tasks.prompt: Order the mutual aid arrangement setup with neighbouring utilities for major sewer events.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the city and three neighbouring utilities agree to share crews, bypass pumps, and vacuum trucks for events beyond one utility capacity.

cards.label: Agree the cost, liability, and supervision arrangements in writing before any event, following each utility approval process
Define the events and request process the arrangement covers, including who may request aid and who may authorize sending it
Correct the incompatibilities the exercise finds, such as fittings or radio channels, and record the fixes in the arrangement file
Review the arrangement annually and after any real deployment, updating contacts, inventories, and lessons
Run a joint field exercise deploying a partner bypass pump at a city station to prove compatibility and the command arrangements
Inventory the shareable resources with their specifications, especially pump connections, hose sizes, and voltage, so aid equipment actually fits

tasks.explanation: Compatibility proven in an exercise is the arrangement, everything else is intention. Writing cost and supervision terms in peacetime prevents the negotiation that otherwise happens during the emergency.

tasks.prompt: Order the basement backup prevention and response program review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: backup events concentrate in three districts, residents expect both prevention work and a fair response when events occur.

cards.label: Analyse the backup record by district and cause, separating mainline surcharge, mainline blockage, and private lateral causes
Check a sample of closed events for whether the cause recorded in the field matches the prevention program the address was assigned to
Report annually to council on backups by cause and district, with the prevention spending and the trend at repeat addresses
Standardize the response to residents, covering the first call script, the field investigation, cleanup guidance, and the claims information provided
Match each district cause to its prevention work, such as capacity projects, cleaning frequency, or backwater valve advice and support
Adjust district programs where the sample shows causes were misclassified and prevention money aimed at the wrong problem

tasks.explanation: Prevention money follows the recorded cause, so misclassification quietly funds the wrong fix, which the sample check hunts for. Repeat addresses are the fairest trend measure, because they show whether specific homes stopped flooding.

tasks.prompt: Order the spill containment and cleanup routine for a sewer overflow on land.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sewage has surfaced from a manhole onto a street and a schoolyard edge, flow is now stopped, and cleanup must protect health and the storm system.

cards.label: Arrange assessment and any disinfection or soil handling the public health guidance in general terms requires for the schoolyard surface
Document the area cleaned, volumes recovered, and the disposal route, and confirm the site is released by the responsible authority before barriers come down
Protect the storm drains and any watercourse path first with berms, covers, and vacuum recovery of ponded sewage
Secure the area with barriers and signage and keep the public, especially children, away from the affected ground
Wash down hard surfaces with the wash water contained and recovered to the sanitary system, never hosed to the storm drains
Recover pooled liquid and visible solids by vacuum truck, working from the clean edge toward the most contaminated area

tasks.explanation: Storm drain protection precedes washing, because cleanup that pushes contamination into the storm system converts one spill into two. Release by the responsible authority, not by appearance, is what reopens a schoolyard.

tasks.prompt: Order an emergency sewer repair decision under a rail crossing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. cards.label: Establish what is known about the pipe condition from records, surface monitoring, and any safe inspection that does not disturb the track bed
Evaluate the repair methods with the railway requirements, comparing trenchless renewal against excavation under the track authority rules
Restrict access at the surface, notify the railway operator through the established contact, and agree any speed or load restrictions they require
Carry out the work under the agreed controls and record the condition found, since it updates the risk picture for the other rail crossings
Set up flow management for the reach, including bypass or storage, sized for the repair options being considered
Agree the method, the monitoring during the work, and the contingency if the void grows or the pipe fails during preparation

tasks.explanation: The railway is notified before engineering debate, because their restrictions shape every option. The condition found feeds the other crossings, since one void under track is evidence about the whole cohort.

tasks.prompt: Order the communications routine for a prolonged overflow affecting a recreation area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow has closed a popular river beach and trail area, the repair will take several days, and public interest is high.

cards.label: Give updates on the promised schedule even when the news is unchanged, and correct any earlier statement that events have overtaken
Reopen only on the agreed water quality and cleanup evidence, announce it through the same channels, and file the communications record with the event file
Post and maintain physical signage at every access point to the closed area, checking daily that signs remain in place
Issue the first public notice through the city channels with the closure, the reason in plain language, and the areas to avoid
