Traffic loading increased that winter and separated the joints
Deep frost heave moved the shallow rigid joints, so renewal there should use depth or flexible joints, not like for like repair

inference.explanation: Depth, joint type, frost reach, soil moisture and prior minor movement all align on heave. Ageing and traffic do not cluster by burial depth in one winter.

nextClue.prompt: Which renewal standard best prevents recurrence?

options.label: Renew shallow failed reaches with flexible joints or deeper burial where road reconstruction allows, prioritised by frost depth exposure
Repair each joint like for like at the same depth and joint type
Renew deep flexible reaches first because they are older

nextClue.explanation: Changing the joint or depth breaks the mechanism that produced the cluster.

clueText.nc-a: The renewal standard specifies flexible joints or depth for shallow exposed reaches.
clueText.nc-b: Like for like repair restores the exact vulnerability that failed.
clueText.nc-c: Deep flexible reaches were the unaffected group in the same winter.

tasks.prompt: A citywide manhole sealing program in a Saskatchewan city is reviewed after one year of paired basin monitoring.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Night flow falls an average of 7 L/s in sealed basins, while matched unsealed basins are unchanged.
Storm peaks in sealed basins are nearly unchanged from before sealing.
Pre program inspection found frame and chimney joint leaks on most sealed manholes, with sound barrels.
Groundwater and rainfall are matched between sealed and control basins through the review year.
No pipe or lateral work was done in either group during the review year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Sealing failed because storm peaks did not fall, so the program should be cancelled
Sealing removed storm inflow, which explains why night flow fell
Sealing removed groundwater infiltration at manholes but did not address fast storm inflow routes
Seasonal groundwater decline explains the drop in sealed basins alone

inference.explanation: Night flow fell only where sealing occurred under matched conditions, while storm peaks held steady. That is an infiltration fix, not an inflow fix or a seasonal artifact.

nextClue.prompt: Which program message best states this result honestly?

options.label: Report the program as a total wet weather success because night flow fell
Report the verified night flow reduction as an infiltration gain, and list storm inflow as a separate remaining target
Report the program as a failure because storm peaks were unchanged

nextClue.explanation: Honest reporting credits the gain actually achieved and keeps the remaining problem visible.

clueText.nc-a: Calling it a total success would hide the unchanged storm peaks.
clueText.nc-b: The report credits 7 L/s of infiltration removal and carries storm inflow forward as open work.
clueText.nc-c: Calling it a failure would discard a verified infiltration gain.

tasks.prompt: Cured in place lining results for a Manitoba basin show a large night flow drop but only a small change in fast storm peaks.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Night flow falls 11 L/s after lining, verified against a control basin.
Fast storm peaks fall only 8 percent at matched rainfall after lining.
Pre lining CCTV showed running joint infiltration along most of the basin mains.
Smoke and dye testing after lining still finds multiple direct storm connections on private property.
The liner passes post installation inspection with sealed connections.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Lining failed, which the small storm peak change proves on its own
The remaining storm peaks come through the new liner wall itself
Night flow fell because the control basin took the treated basin flow
Lining removed the groundwater joint route, while direct private connections still drive the fast storm peaks

inference.explanation: A sound liner, a large night flow drop and persistent tested private connections explain both results. Lining fixed the route it can reach.

nextClue.prompt: Which follow up best addresses the remaining peaks?

options.label: Re-lining the mains to chase the remaining fast peaks
Removing the basin flow meters so peaks are no longer recorded
A private side disconnection program using the smoke and dye results to rank properties

nextClue.explanation: Targeting confirmed private connections addresses the route the evidence identifies.

clueText.nc-a: Re-lining sound pipe cannot disconnect a roof or drain connection.
clueText.nc-b: Removing meters hides peaks instead of reducing them.
clueText.nc-c: The follow up program ranks properties by confirmed dye and smoke results.

tasks.prompt: A lateral renewal pilot renews laterals on one street in a British Columbia town while a matched street keeps its old laterals.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Before the pilot, both streets show similar storm responses and night flows per home.
After renewal, the pilot street storm peak falls 38 percent while the matched street is unchanged.
Main lining, manhole sealing, rainfall and groundwater are the same for both streets.
Lateral cameras before renewal showed cracked laterals with storm connections on the pilot street.
Water billing per home is similar on both streets before and after the pilot.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Lateral renewal caused the pilot street improvement, showing private laterals were a major flow route there
A citywide weather change explains why only the pilot street improved
Lower water use on the pilot street explains the storm peak drop
Main lining explains the difference, even though both streets share the same mains

inference.explanation: Matched streets, shared mains and weather, similar billing, and a drop only on the renewed street isolate laterals as the cause and renewal as the fix.

nextClue.prompt: Which expansion decision best follows?

options.label: Expand lateral renewal to streets with similar camera confirmed lateral defects, keeping matched street checks
Expand main lining instead, since mains are easier to contract
Stop the program because one street is too small a sample to learn from

nextClue.explanation: Expanding where the same defect evidence exists, with controls kept, scales what was proven.

clueText.nc-a: The expansion targets camera confirmed streets and retains a matched comparison street.
clueText.nc-b: Easier contracting does not change which asset the evidence identifies.
clueText.nc-c: A controlled pilot is exactly how a program learns before scaling.

tasks.prompt: A roof disconnection program in an Alberta city claims 400 disconnections, and an audit retests a random sample of the claimed properties.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: City records claim 400 roof leaders disconnected over two program years.
Dye retesting of a random 40 property sample finds 9 leaders reconnected or never disconnected.
Basin storm response falls less than the claimed disconnection count predicted.
The sample was drawn randomly, and retest methods match the original acceptance tests.
Properties with verified disconnections show the expected local flow benefit on street monitoring.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: All 400 disconnections are real, and the retest sample must be wrong
The claimed removal count overstates real removals, so program credit should be based on verified disconnections only
Disconnection never reduces flow, which the verified properties also show
The basin shortfall proves the flow meters failed during the program

inference.explanation: A random retest finds about one in five claims false, verified properties do perform, and basin results fall short by a matching direction. The count, not the method, is overstated.

nextClue.prompt: Which correction best restores program credibility?

options.label: Keep reporting the claimed 400 figure to protect the program reputation
Recount program results from verified disconnections and retest the remaining claimed properties
Cancel disconnection work entirely because the audit found errors

nextClue.explanation: Verified counting keeps council reporting honest while preserving a method that works where it is real.

clueText.nc-a: Reporting a figure the audit showed false would mislead future funding decisions.
clueText.nc-b: The program recounts from verified results and schedules retests for the rest of the claim list.
clueText.nc-c: Verified properties prove the method works, so cancelling it over a counting error wastes a proven tool.

tasks.prompt: A smoke testing program in a prairie town closes most streets, but one basin keeps a fast storm response and the team runs dye follow ups.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Basin storm peaks stay high after smoke testing found and fixed all visible main defects.
Dye tests at six homes show foundation drain dye reaching the sanitary sewer within minutes.
Main and lateral CCTV in the basin shows sound pipes at those six connections.
Streets without foundation drain connections in the same basin show low storm responses.
Rain timing, not groundwater level, predicts the basin storm peaks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The mains are still defective, even though cameras show them sound
Groundwater infiltration explains peaks that track rain timing within minutes
Connected foundation drains are the remaining fast inflow route in this basin
The dye is leaking through soil from the storm system into the sanitary system

inference.explanation: Sound mains, minutes scale dye travel, rain timed peaks and calm streets without such drains point to direct foundation connections. Groundwater cannot respond in minutes.

nextClue.prompt: Which removal step best fits these six properties?

options.label: Line the basin mains a second time to stop the fast peaks
Seal the basin manholes and close the file without property action
Require disconnection of the confirmed foundation drains, with the paired dye and camera file for each address

nextClue.explanation: Address specific confirmed results are the defensible basis for disconnection.

clueText.nc-a: A second lining cannot disconnect a foundation drain.
clueText.nc-b: Manhole sealing does not reach a direct drain connection, and closing the file leaves it active.
clueText.nc-c: Each property file pairs its dye timing with a sound main camera record.

tasks.prompt: A joint grouting program in a Manitoba basin is evaluated joint by joint against pre grouting camera infiltration ratings.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Night flow falls 6 L/s in the grouted basin, while a control basin is unchanged.
Post grouting CCTV shows grouted joints dry, including joints rated as runners before work.
Joints that were skipped because of displacement still weep on post grouting CCTV.
Groundwater levels during before and after checks are closely matched.
No lining, sealing or lateral work was done in the basin during the program.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Grouting failed because some joints in the basin still weep
The night flow drop came from lining done during the same program period
Groundwater decline explains why grouted joints look dry on camera
Grouting sealed the joints it treated, and the skipped displaced joints are the remaining infiltration points

inference.explanation: Treated joints are dry, untreated displaced joints still weep, conditions are matched, and no other work occurred. Grouting worked where it was applied.

nextClue.prompt: Which scope best completes this basin?

options.label: Renew or line the reaches with displaced joints that grouting could not treat, and leave sound grouted reaches in monitoring
Re-grout every joint in the basin, including the dry treated joints
Abandon the basin because grouting did not fix joints it never treated

nextClue.explanation: Completing only the untreated defective reaches spends the remaining budget where water still enters.

clueText.nc-a: The completion scope lists the displaced reaches for renewal and keeps grouted reaches on watch.
clueText.nc-b: Re-grouting dry joints spends money where no water enters.
clueText.nc-c: Abandoning the basin ignores a verified 6 L/s gain and a short remaining list.

tasks.prompt: A basin program in a Saskatchewan city lines mains first, then renews laterals, and measures the gain from each stage separately.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: After main lining alone, storm peaks fall 30 percent and night flow falls 8 L/s.
After lateral renewal on the same basin, storm peaks fall a further 10 percent and night flow a further 2 L/s.
A control basin with no work shows no change across both stages.
Lateral cameras before stage two showed fewer severe defects than the mains had shown before stage one.
Rainfall matching and meter verification are consistent across both stages.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The mains were the larger source in this basin, and lateral work added a smaller real gain after them
Lateral renewal was wasted money because its gain was smaller than the lining gain
Main lining alone would have removed the lateral share as well if given more time
The stage two gain is meter noise, even though the control basin stayed flat

inference.explanation: Staged measurement with a flat control shows both gains are real and the main share was larger. A smaller second gain is still a gain, not waste or noise.

nextClue.prompt: Which sequencing lesson best generalises from this basin?

options.label: Always renew laterals first in every basin regardless of source measurements
Measure each stage separately so future basins can sequence their largest verified source first
Never fund a second stage whose gain is smaller than the first stage

nextClue.explanation: Stage by stage measurement is what lets other basins order work by their own largest source.

clueText.nc-a: A fixed order ignores that source shares differ by basin.
clueText.nc-b: The program guide now requires staged flow checks between main and lateral work.
clueText.nc-c: Refusing smaller second gains would leave verified removable flow in place.

tasks.prompt: Flow monitoring below a shopping district in an Alberta city stays high after sewer work, and catch basin investigations follow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Sewer storm peaks below the district stay high after mains lining and manhole sealing.
Dye placed in three parking lot catch basins appears in the sanitary sewer within minutes.
Camera runs from the catch basin leads show them joining the sanitary main directly.
Catch basins in a control district drain to the storm sewer on dye testing.
Dry weather flow below the district is normal between rain events.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The liner is porous and passes storm water along the whole district reach
Three catch basins are cross connected to the sanitary sewer and drive the remaining storm peaks
Groundwater infiltration explains dye arriving within minutes of placement
Shoppers use far more water during rain, raising true sanitary flow

inference.explanation: Dye timing, camera proof of direct joins, normal dry weather flow and a clean control district identify cross connections. A porous liner cannot move dye in minutes.

nextClue.prompt: Which repair record best closes this finding?

options.label: Line the district mains again and retest the catch basins next year
Seal the catch basin grates so rain cannot enter them at all
Reconnect the three leads to the storm sewer and file the dye timing plus lead camera record for each basin

nextClue.explanation: Documented reconnection removes the proven route and keeps the evidence on file.

clueText.nc-a: Re-lining cannot correct a lead joined to the wrong system.
clueText.nc-b: Sealing grates would flood the parking lots the basins exist to drain.
clueText.nc-c: Each lead is reconnected and its dye and camera record is filed with the repair order.

tasks.prompt: A program verification study in a British Columbia city compares treated and control basins across three matched storms after a combined removal program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian source removal program review. Flows and program records are as stated, in Canadian units.

evidence.label: Across three matched storms, treated basin peaks average 55 percent of dry weather flow above base, down from 180 percent before work.
Control basin peaks average near their before values across the same three storms.
Rainfall depths, groundwater and antecedent conditions are matched storm by storm.
All basin meters pass verification at the start and end of the study.
Sanitary base flow from billing is stable in both basin groups.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Wetter post program weather explains why treated peaks fell while control peaks held
Population decline in treated basins explains the storm peak reduction
The combined program caused the treated basin improvement, because matched controls rule out weather and growth effects
One storm result would have been enough to prove the program effect

inference.explanation: Three matched storms, stable controls, verified meters and stable base flow together support a program effect. Single storms or raw totals could not carry that weight.

nextClue.prompt: Which statement best reports the verified result in general terms?

options.label: State the before and after matched storm response for treated and control basins, without claiming all wet weather flow is gone
State that the program eliminated wet weather flow problems in the city
State only the dollars spent and kilometres treated as the program result

nextClue.explanation: Matched reporting states the achieved reduction accurately and keeps remaining flow visible.

clueText.nc-a: The report shows treated response falling from 180 to 55 percent above base, with controls near unchanged.
clueText.nc-b: Elimination was not achieved, so that claim would be false.
clueText.nc-c: Spending and length are inputs and outputs, not flow outcomes.
